decision_lens: For every code site touching BenchTickContext, IssueBoard, or IssueRegistry, ask: does this run identically — same order, same allocations, same static-init timing — on the flag-off path as it did before Phase 2? A single non-defaulted field, a HashMap traversal not fully resolved by the downstream sort, or an unguarded static touch counts as a world-perturbation regardless of the author's intent, and 'it compiles' is not evidence it's inert.
focus: Rust-level mechanics of the world-inertness claim: every BenchTickContext construction site, OnceLock/Lazy static initialization, HashMap-to-Vec determinism (IssueRegistry sort/dedup), struct/enum changes that could shift existing serialization or hashing, and reachability/ordering of the flag-on emit site relative to the referee and demo's seeds/tick counts.

task_context: Adversarially review this execution-grade implementation plan (Phase 2 of the workipedia->emergence ingestion pipeline, shadowbench-core Rust crate) BEFORE weaker executors (sonnet subagents) build it literally. Core safety claim is WORLD-INERTNESS: a new IssueBoard lives on BenchTickContext (bench-only, cfg(feature=bench)), built once at spawn_bench_loop, EMPTY when the SHADOWBENCH_ISSUE_INGEST env flag is off (empty-when-off discipline copied from cadre/bench_history), surfaced ONLY as a flag-on-only TraceEvent::IssueBoard that NEVER writes the chronicle. The divergence referee (scripts/bench/divergence/referee-issue-ingest.sh) must prove: R1 flag-off byte-identical OLD-vs-NEW (chronicle sha + normalized trace), flag-on chronicle byte-identical to flag-off, and flag-on-trace-minus-issue_board-events == flag-off trace (world-inert), plus a board-engaged guard. Hunt hardest for, and name where each lands (task#/criterion#) + whether it breaks the REFEREE gate, FOG gate, or DEMO + minimal fix: (1) any path where plan code perturbs the FLAG-OFF world and breaks R1 byte-identity — a BenchTickContext construction site not defaulting issue_board, adding a struct field/enum variant that changes serialization/hashing of EXISTING artifacts, a non-deterministic board build (IssueRegistry is a HashMap; board sorts by id — verify airtight), or OnceLock registry init on the flag-off path with an observable side effect. (2) Is the world-inert PROOF valid or circular: does 'flag-on trace minus issue_board == flag-off trace' truly prove inertness, or could board construction (registry OnceLock init, allocations, RNG touch) shift draw-count/draw-order or timing that leaks into the trace even with board events stripped? Is r2-a(flag-on,NEW)-minus-board vs r1-new(flag-off,NEW) the right reference, and is the existing referee's OLD-vs-NEW R1 preserved? Does stripping only event_type==issue_board suffice if the feature changes any other event? (3) Loader correctness: panic-on-invalid (Rust) vs skip+warn (Python generator) mismatch — could committed JSON contain a row the loader rejects? Alias handling + the 353-distinct-count assertion vs alias keys inflating HashMap len. Pillar-map must cover all 16 labels or the loader panics at runtime — guaranteed? Generated-JSON staleness --check guard; include_str! of a stale committed file. (4) Fog parity: is the board truly eval/scorer-side, or could a step leak it into the HQ-visible ledger (recent_reports_json) or agent-visible state? The fog-clean test greps a fixed banned-key list — sufficient? (5) Demo reachability: will 'ai-alignment-crisis' appear in a TICKS=200 flag-on run given the board emits at the initial-roster (BenchStarted) site — is that site reached, is --inline-strategy random correct, referee SEED/TICKS (1000/8766) consistency?
